annotations.description: With 3 mana available (2 Mountains + Riverpyre Verge), Libby could cast either Razorkin Needlehead (RR), Hexing Squelcher (1R), Hired Claw (R), or Tersa Lightshatter (2R). Razorkin Needlehead is a reasonable choice as it punishes card draw and has first strike on your turn, but Hexing Squelcher might be better here since the opponent has Stormchaser's Talent (a Class enchantment that could level up and return spells from graveyard). Squelcher's 'spells you control can't be countered' and ward on other creatures provides protection. However, the strongest consideration is that casting a creature before combat is generally fine when you have no attackers already, and the opponent has an Otter token that's tapped. The real question is whether Tersa Lightshatter would have been better — it costs exactly 2R (3 mana), has haste so it can attack immediately as a 3/3, and its ETB lets you discard up to 2 cards to draw that many, improving hand quality. With haste, Tersa could attack this turn and potentially trigger its graveyard exile ability in future turns. Razorkin Needlehead can't attack profitably this turn into a 1/1 Otter (well, it can with first strike, but the Otter is tapped). Actually both could attack freely since the Otter is tapped. Tersa as a 3/3 haste with card filtering seems stronger than a 2/2 that punishes draws, especially since Tersa's attack trigger becomes relevant with 7+ cards in graveyard later.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Tersa Lightshatter for 2R — it has haste allowing an immediate 3-damage attack, a 3/3 body that's harder to remove, and an ETB that filters your hand (potentially discarding lands or weak cards to find action). This pressures the opponent more immediately and builds toward Tersa's graveyard exile attack trigger.

annotations.description: Playing Tersa Lightshatter before combat is suboptimal when you have Hired Claw and Razorkin Needlehead ready to attack. The opponent has no creatures to block, so attacking first would deal damage and trigger Hired Claw's ability (dealing 1 damage to the opponent since it's a Lizard attacking). After combat, you'd still have 3 mana to cast Tersa. Additionally, Hexing Squelcher might be better here since the opponent appears to be playing a blue-red spells deck (Stormchaser's Talent, Torch the Towers in graveyard) — Squelcher's 'spells you control can't be countered' and ward for your other creatures would protect against countermagic and removal. However, Tersa is a reasonable play for card filtering and board presence.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tersa Lightshatter in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Attack first with Hired Claw and Razorkin Needlehead (opponent has no blockers), then cast Tersa Lightshatter (or Hexing Squelcher) in second main phase. This avoids giving the opponent information before blocks and ensures combat damage triggers happen regardless of what you draw off Tersa.
